userStories.title: Add notifyOrchestrator injectable + pure verdict-line formatter; call from loop.ts review branch
userStories.description: As the sidecar supervisor, I need to invoke a no-op-by-default notifyOrchestrator callback with a formatted verdict line after every non-error review dispatch, so the wiring layer can hand the verdict back to the orchestrator pane without bleeding tmux details into the loop.
acceptanceCriteria: RunSupervisorOptions in src/supervisor/loop.ts declares an optional notifyOrchestrator?: (line: string) => void field. [oracle: grep -Eq 'notifyOrchestrator\?: \(line: string\) => void' src/supervisor/loop.ts]

A pure formatter (formatReviewVerdictLine or equivalent) lives next to the other pure formatters (e.g. in src/supervisor/worker-report.ts or src/supervisor/review.ts) and returns '[cam] review round N: CLEAN', '[cam] review round N: FIXES_PENDING:K', or '[cam] review round N: MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT' depending on the verdict kind. [oracle: grep -Eq 'formatReviewVerdictLine|formatReviewVerdict' src/supervisor/worker-report.ts src/supervisor/review.ts]

After reviewDispatch(uuid) returns in the loop.ts review branch (lines ~942-992), when reviewResult.status !== 'error' and the re-read PRD's prd.review.lastVerdict is non-null, the loop calls opts.notifyOrchestrator?.(formattedLine) before `continue`. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
When opts.notifyOrchestrator is undefined the loop runs unchanged (no throw, no log line). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor]

A unit test in test/supervisor/ pins that the review branch invokes notifyOrchestrator with the exact formatted line for each of the three verdict kinds (CLEAN, FIXES_PENDING:N, MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/loop.ts (review branch lines 942-992; RunSupervisorOptions type around 107-176), src/supervisor/review.ts, src/supervisor/worker-report.ts (mirror formatWorkerReportSummary as the precedent pure formatter), test/supervisor/. Verdict source: re-read PRD's prd.review.lastVerdict after the dispatch (already wired in the existing branch). Keep notifyOrchestrator OPTIONAL; the no-op behavior when absent is what keeps every existing test green. Read scripts/cam/patterns.md (Sidecar-supervisor invariant; tmux mangles TAB / key panes on @cam_label) before touching the loop. Do NOT inject tmux details here: this story is about the contract; US-002 does the wiring.

userStories.title: Wire notifyOrchestrator in host.ts/buildSupervisorOptions via getOrchPaneId + buildWorkerReportSendKeysArgv
userStories.description: As the production sidecar wiring, I need buildSupervisorOptions to resolve the orchestrator pane id and send-keys the verdict line into it, so the verdict actually reaches the orchestrator pane on a real run while staying best-effort when the pane is gone.
acceptanceCriteria: buildSupervisorOptions(cwd) in src/supervisor/host.ts constructs a notifyOrchestrator closure that resolves the orchestrator pane via getOrchPaneId(sessionName, supervisorSpawn) and, if non-null, sends the verdict line via buildWorkerReportSendKeysArgv(orchPane, line). [oracle: grep -q 'notifyOrchestrator' src/supervisor/host.ts]

The closure imports getOrchPaneId from src/tmux/session.ts and buildWorkerReportSendKeysArgv from src/supervisor/worker-report.ts (reused; no new send-keys builder). [oracle: grep -Eq 'getOrchPaneId|buildWorkerReportSendKeysArgv' src/supervisor/host.ts]
When getOrchPaneId returns null, the closure is a silent no-op (no throw, no error log, no send-keys call). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor]
The final opts: RunSupervisorOptions assembled around line ~480 in host.ts sets notifyOrchestrator to this closure. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

A unit test in test/supervisor/ asserts (a) when the fake supervisorSpawn returns a valid orch pane id, the closure invokes send-keys with the argv shape produced by buildWorkerReportSendKeysArgv (no `-l`, Enter as a separate key arg, both in one call); (b) when the fake returns no orch pane, no send-keys is called. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/host.ts (sessionName resolved at ~131; supervisorSpawn at ~161; reviewDispatch construction at ~280; opts at ~480), src/tmux/session.ts (getOrchPaneId), src/supervisor/worker-report.ts (buildWorkerReportSendKeysArgv). Hard rule from patterns.md: send-keys text + Enter MUST go in the SAME tmux call; never use `-l` (CAM-55, sendkeys-literal-enter-gotcha). Best-effort only: getOrchPaneId can legitimately return null (orch pane closed between detection and notify); skip silently. Read patterns.md `@cam_label pane-labeling pattern` and `tmux mangles TAB` before touching tmux args. Do NOT bypass buildSupervisorOptions; the wiring belongs here per the Sidecar dep-wiring invariant.

userStories.title: Real-tmux integration test: verdict line lands in orchestrator pane via the wired closure
userStories.description: As the project's correctness oracle, I need a real-tmux integration test (OS-gated) that proves the end-to-end handback: a CLEAN/FIXES_PENDING/MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT verdict line written by the wired notifyOrchestrator closure actually appears in the orchestrator pane's capture-pane output.
acceptanceCriteria: test/integration/review-verdict-handback.test.ts (or similarly named under test/integration/) exists and follows the existing real-tmux pattern of test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts and test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts (skipped when tmux is absent). [oracle: file-assert: test -f test/integration/review-verdict-handback.test.ts]

The test spins up a real tmux session with an orchestrator pane labeled @cam_label=orchestrator, invokes the production notifyOrchestrator closure (or buildSupervisorOptions output) with a verdict line, and asserts the line is observable via `tmux capture-pane -p` on the orch pane. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The test is OS-gated using the precedent idiom (tmuxAvailable computed via Bun.spawnSync(['tmux','-V']).exitCode===0 and applied via test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable), exactly as in test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts). [oracle: grep -Eq 'Bun\.spawnSync\(\["tmux", "-V"\]\)\.exitCode === 0' test/integration/review-verdict-handback.test.ts && grep -q 'test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable)' test/integration/review-verdict-handback.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Mirror: test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts and test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts (skip pattern, real-tmux setup/teardown). The exact skip idiom from sendkeys-submit.test.ts:18,30 is `const tmuxAvailable = Bun.spawnSync(["tmux", "-V"]).exitCode === 0;` and `test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable)(...)`; the AC3 oracle pins both literals. Lesson reinforced by CAM-55 operator smoke (patterns.md): a unit fake that returns the output the code EXPECTS cannot catch tool-real-behavior bugs; every new tmux send-keys integration MUST be guarded by a real-tmux test. Cleanup the session in afterEach (kill-session). Use a unique session name per test invocation to avoid collisions with a live `cam run`.

userStories.title: Structured supervisor event for the verdict handback in cam-worker-events.jsonl
userStories.description: As the operator reviewing post-run logs, I need a structured event line in .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl every time the sidecar pushes a review verdict back to the orchestrator, so the handback is auditable independently of the pane scrollback.
acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/events.ts (or wherever event kinds are declared) gains a new event kind for the review verdict handback (e.g. 'review-verdict-handback' or similar) carrying at minimum { verdict, round }. [oracle: grep -Eq 'review-verdict|verdict.*handback|handback' src/supervisor/events.ts]
The loop.ts review branch emits this event via the existing logEvent pattern after the verdict is known and (when applicable) after notifyOrchestrator is called. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

A unit test asserts the event is emitted (captured via an injected event sink or by reading the jsonl path used in tests) with the correct verdict kind and round number for at least one of CLEAN / FIXES_PENDING / MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/events.ts (existing event kinds; grep `logEvent` in loop.ts for emission precedents like outcome-fallback and sidecar-exit), src/supervisor/loop.ts (emission site colocated with the notifyOrchestrator call from US-001), test/supervisor/. Per scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md: the event log is supervisor-owned and append-only; do NOT have the agent hand-write into it. Reuse the existing logEvent helper signature; do not invent a new write path.

userStories.title: Push BLOCKED line on review dispatch 'blocked' path so the orchestrator never hangs on a failed review
userStories.description: As the operator, I need a one-line `[cam] review BLOCKED: <detail>` pushed to the orchestrator pane when the review dispatch reaches 'blocked' (pane died after retries / timed out), so the orchestrator narrates the blocker instead of hanging.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/supervisor/loop.ts at the existing blocked-review path (lines ~970-974, where notifyTerminal('blocked') runs before `return`), the loop calls opts.notifyOrchestrator?.('[cam] review BLOCKED: <detail>') with a short detail (e.g. the reason returned by the dispatch). [oracle: grep -q '\[cam\] review BLOCKED' src/supervisor/loop.ts]
The call is best-effort (no throw if notifyOrchestrator is absent or fails). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor]
A unit test pins that the blocked-path invokes notifyOrchestrator exactly once with a string starting with `[cam] review BLOCKED:`. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/loop.ts (blocked path lines 970-974; reuses the notifyOrchestrator injectable from US-001), test/supervisor/. Keep the BLOCKED detail short (single line); the orchestrator narrates from the pane, not from a structured payload. Do not introduce a separate injectable for blocked: reuse notifyOrchestrator so the optionality story is consistent. The pure formatter from US-001 can be extended (one function or two: judgment call, both fine as long as they live next to formatWorkerReportSummary).
